suppress.notes:
file name: jsonschema2pojo-core-1.2.2.jar
org.jsonschema2pojo:jsonschema2pojo-core is pulled in transitively by the `org.jsonschema2dataclass` Gradle plugin; it is not a directly declared dependency. The CVE is fixed in jsonschema2pojo 1.3.0, but that fix is NOT yet consumable here: plugin 6.1.0 (the latest release, published Jan 2026) still pins jsonschema2pojo 1.2.2, and the upstream bump to 1.3.3 is still an open PR (jsonschema2dataclass/js2d-gradle#1159). The plugin releases roughly annually in January, so this suppression is dated Jan 2027 to coincide with the next expected release. Rated MEDIUM (VulDB CVSS 4.0 4.8 / CVSS 3.1 5.3, vector AV:L requiring local access). Not exploitable here: (1) This is a BUILD-TIME ONLY dependency. It resolves solely in the `jsonschema2dataclass` and `jsonschema2dataclassPlugins` configurations, consumed by the code generation task generateJsonSchema2DataClassConfigMain. It is absent from both runtimeClasspath and compileClasspath, so it is never packaged into the container image and never executed by the running service. (2) The attack requires a maliciously crafted yaml schema, which would require write access to the source code. Our only inputs are the schemas checked in under src/main/resources/yamlschema, and they do not result in this issue. (3) The underlying defect is a StackOverflowError when a schema root is self-referencing (fixed upstream by joelittlejohn/jsonschema2pojo#1679). On the JVM this fails the build rather than corrupting memory, despite the "stack-based buffer overflow" wording used by the reporting CNA. REMOVE this suppression once an org.jsonschema2dataclass release adopting jsonschema2pojo >= 1.3.0 is published and upgraded to.

file name: commons-lang-2.6.jar
CVE-2025-48924 (CWE-674, uncontrolled recursion) is a StackOverflowError thrown by ClassUtils.getClass(...) on very long inputs. It affects commons-lang:commons-lang 2.0 to 2.6 and org.apache.commons:commons-lang3 3.0 before 3.18.0. Our directly declared commons-lang3 is 3.20.0 and is NOT affected; this finding is the LEGACY commons-lang 2.x artifact, pulled in transitively by org.jsonschema2pojo:jsonschema2pojo-core:1.2.2 via the `org.jsonschema2dataclass` Gradle plugin. See the suppression above for why that plugin cannot currently be upgraded. There is NO fixed release to upgrade to. 2.6 is the final release of the 2.x line on Maven Central, and the ASF confirmed on LANG-1781 that only the 3.x line is maintained. A non-recursive rewrite was merged to the LANG_2_X branch (apache/commons-lang#1492) in November 2025 but has never been released, so pinning is not an option. Rated LOW by the ASF (CISA-ADP CVSS 3.1 5.3, vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/C:N/I:N/A:L - availability only). Not exploitable here: (1) This is a BUILD-TIME ONLY dependency. It resolves solely in the `jsonschema2dataclass` and `jsonschema2dataclassPlugins` configurations, consumed by the code generation task generateJsonSchema2DataClassConfigMain. It is absent from both runtimeClasspath and compileClasspath (which resolve commons-lang3 3.20.0), so it is never packaged into the container image and never executed by the running service. (2) Triggering it requires passing an extremely long, attacker-controlled class name to ClassUtils.getClass. Our only codegen inputs are the schemas checked in under src/main/resources/yamlschema, so this would require write access to the source code. (3) The impact is a StackOverflowError, which on the JVM fails the build rather than corrupting memory; there is no confidentiality or integrity impact. REMOVE this suppression once an org.jsonschema2dataclass release adopting a jsonschema2pojo version that drops the legacy commons-lang 2.x dependency is published and upgraded to. Dated to coincide with the plugin's next expected (annual, January) release, as above.

org.hdrhistogram:HdrHistogram is pulled in transitively via Micrometer (used by Spring Boot Actuator metrics); it is not a directly declared dependency. Both CVEs affect HdrHistogram up to 2.2.2, are rated LOW (VulDB CVSS 4.0 1.9 / CVSS 3.1 3.3, vector AV:L requiring local access), and are officially DISPUTED for lack of a crossed security boundary. Neither is exploitable here: (1) CVE-2026-14683 (CWE-400/CWE-789) is uncontrolled memory allocation in AbstractHistogram.decodeFromCompressedByteBuffer, reachable only when decoding an attacker-controlled compressed histogram byte buffer with a manipulated lengthOfCompressedContents. This service never deserialises/decodes external histogram data; Micrometer only encodes its own internally-produced metrics. (2) CVE-2026-14686 is an incorrect comparison / improper input validation in DoubleHistogram.recordValue ("Range Check"), reachable only when recording attacker-controlled values through that API, which this service does not expose. There is currently NO fixed release (all versions up to 2.2.2 are affected and the project has not responded), so pinning is not an option. REMOVE this suppression once a fixed HdrHistogram release is published and adopted transitively by Micrometer.

CVE-2026-47838 is an X.509 certificate CN parsing flaw in Spring Security's SubjectDnX509PrincipalExtractor, which can cause the wrong username to be read and allow user impersonation. Not applicable here for two independent reasons: (1) Already fixed in our version. This service resolves Spring Security 7.1.1 via the Spring Boot 4.1.1 BOM. The advisory (https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47838) states it is "a continuation of CVE-2026-22747, which addressed this same issue for Spring Security 7.0.x", so the 7.x line was patched first. Affected versions stop at 6.5.10 / 6.4.17 / 6.3.17 / 5.8.26 / 5.7.24; 7.x is not affected. (2) The vulnerable code path is unused. SubjectDnX509PrincipalExtractor only applies to X.509 client-certificate authentication. This service authenticates with JWT bearer tokens via spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server and configures no X.509/mTLS authentication. Note also that VMware score this 6.8 rather than NVD's 8.1, because the extractor sits behind the pre-authentication flow and exploitation "presupposes a compromise of that upstream trust". REMOVE this suppression if dependency-check stops reporting it, or revisit if this service ever adopts X.509 client-certificate authentication.

FALSE POSITIVE: we are already on a fixed version. CVE-2026-47842 is a deterministic AES/CBC encryption flaw in Spring Security's AesBytesEncryptor (all-zero IV). The advisory (https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47842) lists 7.1.0 as the only affected release on the 7.1.x line, and this service resolves Spring Security 7.1.1 via the Spring Boot 4.1.1 BOM. Dependency-check still reports it because the CVE is in "Awaiting Analysis" state with no CPE version ranges published, so there is no machine-readable "fixed at 7.1.1" boundary to match on. REMOVE this suppression once dependency-check stops reporting it.

CVE-2026-53914 affects Kotlin before 2.4.20. If Kotlin reads build cache metadata that someone has tampered with, it can run their code. The application we ship is not affected, because we build with Kotlin 2.4.20 and runtimeClasspath resolves kotlin-stdlib, kotlin-stdlib-jdk8 and kotlin-reflect at 2.4.20. The warning comes from two parts of the Gradle build that still use older Kotlin jars: (1) ktlint. (2) kotlinAbiValidationCompatClasspath. These are build time only. An attacker would need local access with high privileges to tamper with the build cache. REMOVE when EROPSPT-786 replaces ktlint (which removes the 2.2.21 downgrade) and the Kotlin Gradle plugin stops pinning 2.4.0 build tools.
